target_customer: Crypto exchanges, custodians and other virtual asset service providers that must comply with the FATF Travel Rule
problem: New global rules required crypto businesses to exchange sender and receiver information and vet counterparties like banks, with no standard way to do it across providers.
business_model: B2B SaaS and network for Travel Rule compliance and counterparty due diligence, later stablecoin payments products

founders.name: Pelle Braendgaard
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in the company seed announcement; the team previously worked together at uPort. Not listed on the YC page opened.

founders.name: Ania Lipinska
founders.background_notes: UX designer, listed as founder on the YC page.

competitors.name: CipherTrace
competitors.what: Crypto analytics firm that released software for sharing customer data under the FATF Travel Rule

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed secure data exchange, identity and address verification and integrations with many exchanges, standard engineering with protocol and interoperability challenges.

defensibility.rationale: A network of connected institutions and compliance workflow integration create lock-in once adopted, but several vendors and open protocols competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Analytics firms and protocol groups entered the Travel Rule space around 2019 to 2021; Notabene stayed independent and raised a Series B in November 2024.

market_need_then: FATF guidance of June 2019 required virtual asset service providers to pass originator and beneficiary data, with enforcement expected over the following year, per the YC description.

branding.domain_note: Uses notabene.id, not a .com, per the company site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Institutional trust language: the open trust layer for global payments

brand_strength.rationale: Positioning around trust is consistent, but no press about the brand itself was found; the name is a Latin phrase meaning note well, though no source states that was intended.

pivots.to: Travel Rule plus stablecoin payments platform (Notabene Flow)
pivots.why: Series B announcement framed the raise around stablecoins and payments

outcome_analysis: Notabene rode the FATF Travel Rule deadline, raising a seed in November 2020, a $10.2M Series A in November 2021 and a $14.5M Series B in November 2024. Founders came from uPort and ConsenSys with identity and crypto experience, and the company claims a network of over 2,000 institutions. Competition from analytics vendors and open protocols stayed intense.
notes: Seed article gives total 2.3M to date, so about 0.5M of earlier money is not itemized. Coinspeaker states 12M total to date, conflicting. Seed was reported as 1.76M by one outlet and 1.765M by the company. Sygna was a competitor but no source dated near the batch was found. Founding year 2020 inferred from a seed article saying six months after founding; not directly stated by YC.
